task.description: Document the WF03-ISS-0175 run: changelog entries for ISS-0175 (GH #503) and ISS-0177 (GH #506); verify whether any requirement maps to these build-infrastructure fixes; file the unaddressed third acceptance criterion of ISS-0175 (clean-checkout CI job) as its own issue and forward it to the global queue; mark both fixed issues RESOLVED with resolution and prevention text.
acceptance_criteria: CHANGELOG.md documents both fixes and references GH #503 and #506
Requirement-status claim verified against docs/requirements.yaml rather than assumed
ISS-0178 registered, filed on GitHub with rco-sync-ref marker, and added to the global queue
ISS-0175 and ISS-0177 are RESOLVED with resolution + prevention text

result.summary: CHANGELOG.md documents both defects under [Unreleased] Fixed, referencing GH #503 and #506, including why tracking luajit_relver.txt matches upstream intent (upstream's Makefile falls back to a tracked ../.relver for non-git consumers) and the real-git-clone evidence (71/71 test-lua, no regression at 936/1000). No requirement status change was needed, and this was verified rather than assumed: all 359 entries in docs/requirements.yaml were searched and none maps to these build-infrastructure fixes, so no reqctl set-status/render-status was run. ISS-0175's third acceptance criterion (a clean-checkout CI job) is NOT met by this run and was filed as ISS-0178 / GH #507 after collision-checking, then queued via queue_add.py. ISS-0175 and ISS-0177 are both RESOLVED with resolution, verification and prevention text; all three are recorded in issue_index.json.

issues.description: ISS-0175 acceptance criterion 3 (clean-checkout CI job exercising test-lua) is not addressed by this run. Filed as ISS-0178 / GH #507 and queued for its own WF-03 run per the Unblock-Everything scope boundary.

Pre-existing, not caused by this run: docs/issues/issue_index.json had drifted — its entries stopped at ISS-0152 and next_issue_id was 153 while ISS-0166..ISS-0177 already existed on disk. This run appended its own three issues but did not backfill the missing entries or correct next_issue_id, since that is unrelated to the defects being fixed.
